memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: At that time the Lord said to Joshua, "Make flint knives and circumcise the Israelites again." So Joshua made flint knives and circumcised the Israelites at Gibeath Haaraloth. — Josh 5:2-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Right on the edge of the Promised Land, with enemies nearby and Jericho ahead, God gives a surprising command: not "prepare for battle," but "renew the covenant sign." Circumcision was the mark God had given Abraham, the sign that this was a people who belonged to Him. It had to be restored before Israel could move forward.

There is deep wisdom here. Before the conquest, God calls His people back to their identity as those set apart for Him. He wanted them to remember whose they were before they fought a single battle. Right relationship with God comes before great work for God. Our first business is always to be His.

We must handle this passage honestly. Circumcision was a specific sign of the old covenant with Israel; it is not a command for Christians today. The New Testament is clear that physical circumcision does not save and is not required of believers (Gal 5:6; Col 2:11). So we do not copy the ritual — but we do learn the principle behind it.

For that outward sign pointed to an inward reality: God wants a people whose hearts are set apart to Him, a "circumcision of the heart, by the Spirit" (Rom 2:29). In Christ, God has cut away our old sinful nature and marked us as His own. Before we rush into the work God gives, He calls us first to remember that we belong to Him, heart and soul.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you put "being God's" before "doing for God," or is it the other way around?
2. What does it mean for your heart to be "set apart" for God today?
3. How does belonging to God shape the way you face the challenges ahead?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, remind me that I belong to You before I do anything for You. Set my heart apart, and mark me as Your own by Your Spirit. Amen.
